2.text: his wife. The wives of “house-spirits” are also supposed to have clandestine

3.text: lovers among the “reˊkkeñ-spirits” that roam about.

4.text: Another man, of the Kolyma country, called his “house-spirit” Wolvaˊᵋ-

5.text: laˊul (“motionless man”), and his wife Wuˊlve-ñeˊut (“motionless woman”).

6.text: “House-spirits” live in the dark storage-place in the rear of the tent

7.text: (yaˊñan). At night they come out around the corners of the sleeping-room.

8.text: They receive a small share of every larger sacrifice, which is placed on

9.text: the ground, near the corners of the sleeping-room.

10.text: Some of the “Beings” have so-called “assistants” (vɪˊyolɪt). For instance,

11.text: the Creator, or the Spirit of the Zenith, has an “assistant,” who was described

12.text: to me as having a raven’s head. This feature is evidently connected with

13.text: the Raven myth.¹ The “assistant” receives a part of the sacrifices that are

14.text: directed upward. On account of his beak he is called “Raven’s-Beak”

15.text: (Valvɪyaˊk). In one sketch (Fig. 225, a) he is represented as having a

16.text: raven’s beak painted on his face. On

17.text: another sketch made on a board with a

18.text: sharp instrument (Fig. 225, b) he is repre-

19.text: sented as having a raven’s head and feet,

20.text: one wing, and one human hand.

21.text: The Raven mentioned in different in-

22.text: cantations is also supposed to be Valvɪyaˊk,

23.text: “assistant” to the Creator or to the Zenith.

24.text: According to the shamans, he usually as-

25.text: sumes the shape of a raven, and lives in

26.text: the region of the sky, near the Polar Star. This region abounds with worms

27.text: of a peculiar kind (not the one mentioned on p. 311), which form a part of

28.text: his food. When called by shamans to cure their patients, he devours the

29.text: disease as a bird devours worms. One of the shamans, however, distinguished

30.text: between this Raven and the Raven who restored to the earth the sources

31.text: of light. The latter was called by him a very mighty “Being,” who had dea-

32.text: lings with mankind only at the time of the creation, but, after that, transfor-

33.text: med himself into thunder, and became invisible.

34.text: Kereˊtkun has an “assistant,” who has a wife of his own. I could not

35.text: ascertain his name, perhaps he has none. He is always mentioned as Kereˊt-

36.text: kun’s “assistant.” He supervises the construction of Kereˊtkun’s boats. Special

37.text: sacrifices and ceremonials are made for him. These will be described later.

38.text: Even keˊlet and other spirits occasionally have “assistants.” In one of

39.text: the sketches, such an “assistant” is represented crawling on his knees toward

40.text: a victim that he wants to kill for his master.

41.text: The name vɪˊyolɪn is also applied in incantations to various “spirits” who

42.text: are called to give help. For instance, the man repeating an incantation says,
